newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Mediterranean countries to connect power grids.
newsitem.headline: Mediterranean countries to connect power grids.

text.p: Spain and Morocco as well as Egypt and Libya will link their power grids by the end of the year in a step towards full connection between northern and southern Mediterranean countries, officials said on Wednesday.

Energy ministers from Algeria, Libya, Tunisia, Italy, Egypt and Morocco and a Spanish representative meeting in Tunis were also told a tender would be issued by the end of 1997 to link Tunisia and Libya by the year 2000.
The link would then run from Egypt to Libya, Tunisia, Algeria, Morocco and Spain, which is connected to the European grid.

"The power connection between Morocco and Spain will be switched on during the second half of this year," Moroccan Energy Minister Abdellatif Guerraoui told the Ministerial Conference for Connecting Power Grids in the Mediterranean.
Spain said the connection, which would enable it to provide Morocco with electricity, would be completed by September through a 26-km (16-mile) submarine cable.
Egypt and Libya said a link from the Egyptian city of Salloum to the Libyan city of Tobruk would also be completed by the end of the year.
A conference report obtained by Reuters said international advisers had been asked to prepare technical requirements for issuing a tender by July for the Libyan-Tunisian link.
It said the cost was estimated at about $130 million, to be financed partly by a $66 million loan from the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development.
Tunisian Industry Minister Slaheddine Bouguerra proposed that his country and Italy revive a project discussed in 1989 to link their grids under the Mediterranean.
He said several Mediterranean countries had expressed a wish to join the group and proposed that France, Portugal, Greece and Mauritania be invited to the next conference.
Italian Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani said there was a project to link Egypt to Greece through the Mediterranean to complete the regional connection.
He said such cooperation was needed because of the volume of investment required to meet energy demand in the region.
